title: Birgitzköpfl & Axamer Lizum
name: Birgitzköpfl & Axamer Lizum
kurzbeschreibung: The Birgitzköpfl at 2,039 m in the Axamer Lizum near Innsbruck: spectacular panoramic mountain at the foot of the Kalkkögel with scenic trails and via ferratas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The distinctive Birgitzköpfl rises to an altitude of 2,039 metres as a beloved scenic and hiking summit in the world-renowned Axamer Lizum in Tyrol's Innsbruck-Land district. Located just 20 kilometres southwest of the provincial capital Innsbruck, the mountain forms the gateway to the rugged limestone pinnacles of the Kalkkögel – often heralded as the "North Tyrolean Dolomites". Offering expansive views over the Tyrolean Inntal, the Stubai Alps, and the sheer rock faces of the Schlicker Seeschneid, the Birgitzköpfl captivates mountaineers, hikers, and nature lovers alike.

Hiking Paradise & Kalkkögel View

The Axamer Lizum achieved international renown as the two-time host venue of the Olympic Winter Games (1964 and 1976). In summer, this high-alpine arena transforms into a colorful floral and hiking haven. From the Birgitzköpfl, diverse hiking itineraries unfold for every level of experience: one of the most popular scenic tours is the descent past the Birgitzköpflhaus and the Birgitzer Alm through dense stone pine forests and alpine rose-covered slopes. For ambitious mountaineers, the summit marks the starting point for the challenging traverse of the Kalkkögel via the Widdersberg and the Malgrubenscharte. Via ferrata climbers appreciate the modern secured climbing routes traversing the rocky flanks of surrounding peaks. In early summer, the steep grassy slopes around the Birgitzköpfl blaze in the rich pink blossoms of countless alpine roses.

Visit & Getting There

The Birgitzköpfl is freely and openly accessible year-round free of charge via alpine hiking trails; during the summer season from early July to late September, the modern 10-seater gondola Hoadlbahn operates in the Axamer Lizum, from whose mountain station the Birgitzköpfl can be reached via a high-alpine trail. The rustic Birgitzköpflhaus (2,035 m) provides traditional Tyrolean hut meals and overnight accommodation for hikers during the summer. Getting there by car: from Innsbruck via Götzens and Axams along the regional road up into the Axamer Lizum (large free car park right at the road terminus at 1,580 m). By public transport: from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, VVT bus route 4162 runs hourly directly into the Axamer Lizum.

Tips

The hiking trails to the Birgitzköpfl navigate alpine terrain and require sturdy hiking boots with good tread as well as surefootedness. Stop by the Birgitzköpflhaus to enjoy homemade Tyrolean Kaiserschmarrn with cranberries on the sun terrace with unobstructed views of the jagged peaks of the Kalkkögel.
